newsitem.title: CANADA: CS Resources intensifies alliance talks.
newsitem.headline: CS Resources intensifies alliance talks.

text.p: CS Resources Ltd, faced with a pending C$413 million takeover bid from Gulf Canada Resources Ltd, has intensified its efforts to strike a strategic alliance with another company, CS Chief Executive Dennis Sharp said on Monday.

"We're moving as quickly as we can and it would be presumptuous of me to say when we might make an announcement. But we all know that the clock is ticking," Sharp told Reuters in a telephone interview.
"We are working very diligently on that...and we are taking into account the need to assess the short term as well as the long term in maximizing shareholder value," he said.

Sharp declined to identify CS's prospective strategic partner, but said talks started before Gulf announced it planned to bid for the high-tech heavy oil producer on Friday, and intensified over the weekend.
Gulf said it planned to offer CS shareholders either C$14.50 in cash, subject to a maximum cash portion of C$100 million, or 1.1539 Gulf shares for each CS share.

Sharp said he could not give his opinion of the value of CS until financial adviser Gordon Capital performed its due diligence in light of the Gulf bid. But he suggested the company's future appeared bright amid several heavy oil and oil sands operations and opportunities.
His hiring of Dee Parkinson, the former head of Suncor Energy Inc's oil sands group, as president, demonstrated his high expectations for the firm, said Sharp, who founded the company in the 1980s.
Parkinson was set to take over as CEO in August.
